newsitem.title: RWANDA: Multinational force soldiers to help refugees.
newsitem.headline: Multinational force soldiers to help refugees.

text.p: The Canadian commander of a proposed multinational force said air drops of aid to eastern Zaire would only be used as a last resort and the force's first troops would go in on foot with aid workers on Friday.
Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril said rebel Zairean leader Laurent Kabila told him in talks earlier on Thursday in the rebel-held city of Goma he saw no need for any multinational force to intervene.

"It is a humanitarian (mission), which has nothing to do politically or militarily and that is what I told the one who is controlling the ground," Baril told reporters before leaving Kigali late on Thursday for the force's headquarters at Entebbe airport, Uganda.
He said he hoped air drops by his force would be authorised because he wanted to have "this tool in my back pocket if we ever find an emergency somewhere we can react very quickly".
"But let me tell you it (air drops) is complex, it is dangerous, it is very difficult and we use it in the last resort.
"First of all we have got to find out where they (refugees) are, how many and in what condition and that is what we have been working on," he said.

"We have foot patrols going tomorrow with the humanitarian (agencies) and I am willing to help them with my soldiers to go on the ground unarmed," he said, without clearly saying whether troops would be going into rebel-held areas of eastern Zaire.
"It is urgent that we find out how to sort out this mess as soon as we can," he added.
Baril said he would discuss in detail Zaire's rejection of air drops with officials in Kinshasa on Saturday or Sunday.
He said Kabila made it easy for him to go to the town of Sake, west of the Zairean city of Goma, and in the area he saw some of 40,000 refugees heading towards the Rwandan border.

"There's 40,000 refugees in fairly good shape. They are very determined, they are tired and they are hungry but they are being fed along the road by the humanitarians (aid workers) who have control," he said.
"There are medical stations and the head of the column has passed Sake heading for Goma and they should start coming in probably early in the morning (on Friday)," the general said.
He said Kabila said he did not see the situation required a multinational force in Zaire "but I discussed with him all the options that I have if we are so authorised by member states".
He said he had also discussed with Kabila the possibility of using Goma airport but said he would only tell journalists about the result of his talks if there was a need to use it.
Baril's day-long trip on Thursday by road from the Rwandan capital Kigali to Goma and Sake in eastern Zaire was his first to the swathe of territory controlled by Kabila's rebel forces.

Kabila has said there are very few Rwandan and Burundian refugees in rebel-held territory because most have gone home to Rwanda. He says an international military presence would only serve to prop up Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Baril, commander of Canada's ground forces, was appointed in mid-November to head the multinational force to bring aid to refugees who have dispersed because of fighting in east Zaire.
The Zairean government says it will only allow supplies into its territory for Zaireans displaced within their own country and not for refugees from Rwanda.
Baril said on Wednesday night Rwandan military strongman Major-General Paul Kagame, who is vice president and defence minister, had told him he saw little reason for his force.
The Rwandan government says any multinational force for Zaire is irrelevant as most Rwandan refugees have come home.
Rwandan officials have said the force cannot use Rwandan territory as a base for operations following the return of an estimated 600,000 Rwandan refugees in five days from November 15.
But the U.N. refugee agency says hundreds of thousands of refugees and displaced Zaireans remain in eastern Zaire and need help.
